Underrepresented in Medicine Variables-
URM variable vs URM_AAMC : The URM variable provides higher overall representation of underrepresented in medicine students within the cohort compared to the stricter criteria (URM_AAMC). I suggest we use the URM variable in analysis for preventing small sample size limitations, maintaining adequate statistical power, and allowing for a more robust comparative evaluation.

```{r, echo=FALSE}

summary(df$URM)

```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
summary(df$URM_AAMC)
```

OSCE Variables-

OSCE: PI mentioned that they are most interested in the Communication and Physical examination OSCE exam scores, these will be treated as primary outcomes. OSCE scores were aggregated across component (communication, physical examination, medical documentation, or oral)



```{r, echo=FALSE}
#---Osce missingness table------##
miss_tbl <- df %>%
  select(URM, all_of(ordered_osce)) %>%
  summarise(across(-URM, list(n_miss = ~sum(is.na(.x)),
                                  pct_miss = ~round(mean(is.na(.x)) * 100, 1)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("variable", ".value"),
               names_pattern = "(.*)_(n_miss|pct_miss)") %>%
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = c(ordered_osce, "STEP1_ExamScore", "STEP2CK_ExamScore"))) %>%
  arrange(variable)

miss_tbl
```

This table above summarizes the missing data analysis, showing the count (n_miss) and percentage (pct_miss) of missing values for various OSCE component scores and exam metrics. Across the listed variables, missingness ranges from `r min(miss_tbl$n_miss)` to `r max(miss_tbl$n_miss)` observations, representing roughly `r min(miss_tbl$pct_miss)`% to `r max(miss_tbl$pct_miss)`% of the dataset.



```{r, echo=FALSE}

#Checking OSCE missingness per cases(rows) to figure out if there's anything weird or that we have to change
# ---- 1. Number of missing OSCE scores per student ----
osce_missing <- df %>%
  mutate(n_osce_miss = rowSums(is.na(across(all_of(ordered_osce)))),
         pct_osce_miss = round(n_osce_miss / length(ordered_osce) * 100, 1))


all_n_osce_missing <- osce_missing %>% count(n_osce_miss) %>% mutate(pct = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1))

all_n_osce_missing


```

This table above evaluates missing OSCE scores at the student level, showing that the majority of students `r max(all_n_osce_missing$n[all_n_osce_missing$n_osce_miss == 0])` students, or (`r max(all_n_osce_missing$pct[all_n_osce_missing$n_osce_miss == 0])`%) have complete data with zero missing scores. Across the remaining students, missing OSCE counts range from `r min(all_n_osce_missing$n_osce_miss[all_n_osce_missing$n_osce_miss > 0])` to `r max(all_n_osce_missing$n_osce_miss)` missing items (16 missing items = all OSCE component scores).




```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Filter out students with completely missing OSCE data (16 missing scores)
df_clean <- osce_missing %>% 
  filter(n_osce_miss < max(n_osce_miss))

```

After excluding `r nrow(osce_missing) - nrow(df_clean)` students who lacked complete OSCE data, the analytical sample for the new dataframe (df_clean) was reduced to a sample size of N = `r nrow(df_clean)`.



```{r, echo=FALSE}
df_clean %>% 
  filter(URM == "unknown") %>% 
  select(URM, URM_AAMC, amcasEthnicityDesc, amcas_othethnicity, additional_ethnicity, race_desc, race_cat_desc, additional_race)

```


The above table confirms that 6 students actively declined to report their race/ethnicity on their applications, making it impossible to categorize their URM status and justifying their exclusion from the final analytical sample.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
df_final <- df_clean %>% 
  filter(URM != "unknown")
```
After excluding `r nrow(df_clean) - nrow(df_final)` students with unknown URM status, the final analytical sample comprised N = `r nrow(df_final)` students.



```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Table 1 stratified by URM status
df_final %>%
  mutate(URM = droplevels(URM),
         gender = droplevels(gender)) %>%
  select(
    URM, 
    gender, 
    STEP1_ExamScore, 
    STEP2CK_ExamScore, 
    all_of(ordered_osce),
  ) %>% 
  tbl_summary(
    by = URM,
    type = list(
      all_of(c(
        "P1SprBates_CommScore", 
        "P2FallRamos_CommScore", 
        "P2FallRamos_OralPresScore", 
        "P2SpringSnelling_CommScore"
      )) ~ "continuous"
    ),
    statistic = list(
      all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({sd})",
      all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)"
    ),
    digits = all_continuous() ~ 1,
    missing = "no"
  ) %>%
  add_overall() %>%
  bold_labels() |> 
  modify_footnote(all_stat_cols() ~ "Mean (SD); n (%)")
```


Table 1 above: Baseline demographic characteristics, standardized examination scores (USMLE Step 1 and Step 2 CK), and OSCE performance metrics were summarized overall and stratified by URM status. Continuous variables are presented as mean (SD) and categorical variables as n (%).


```{r, echo=FALSE}
osce_stat_table <- df_final |> 
  summarise(across(all_of(ordered_osce), 
                   list(
                     Mean = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     SD   = ~sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     Median = ~median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     IQR  = ~IQR(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     Min  = ~min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     Max  = ~max(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     N    = ~sum(!is.na(.x))
                   ))) |> 
  # Pivot longer safely by splitting at the *last* underscore
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = c("OSCE_Exam", "Statistic"),
    names_pattern = "^(.*)_(Mean|SD|Median|IQR|Min|Max|N)$"
  ) |> 
  # Pivot wider using the correct 'value' column name generated by pivot_longer
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Statistic,
    values_from = value
  )
#osce_stat_table
```


```{r, echo=FALSE}
osce_stat_table_urm <- df_final |>

                     IQR  = ~IQR(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     Min  = ~min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     Max  = ~max(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     N    = ~sum(!is.na(.x))
                   ))) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -URM,
    names_to = c("OSCE_Exam", "Statistic"),
    names_pattern = "^(.*)_(Mean|SD|Median|IQR|Min|Max|N)$"
  ) |> 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Statistic,
    values_from = value
  )

#osce_stat_table_urm
```

Constructed OSCE variables represent the mean of the Bates, Ramos, Payne, Hyde, and Snelling scores for each evaluation component. For each student, available pre-clerkship OSCE scores were averaged across cases and semesters separately for communication, physical examination, medical documentation, and oral presentation.

```{r, echo=FALSE}

# I had AI help with this code below. I used Gemini 3 to help me with combining of 
# groups with grepl. I also used grepl documentation to double check other arguments I could use. 
# grepl documentation https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/base/versions/3.6.2/topics/grep


df_categorized <- df_final |> 
  filter(URM %in% c("Non-URM", "URM")) |> 
  select(URM, all_of(ordered_osce)) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -URM,
    names_to = "Exam_Name",
    values_to = "Score"
  ) |> 
  # Create a grouped category based on keywords in the exam names
  mutate(Competency = case_when(
    grepl("Comm", Exam_Name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Communication Score",
    grepl("Phys|Physical", Exam_Name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Physical Exam Score",
    grepl("Med|Doc", Exam_Name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Medical Documentation",
    grepl("Oral|Pres", Exam_Name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Oral Presentation",
    TRUE ~ "Other" # Catch-all for any remaining exams
  ))


competency_summary <- df_categorized |> 
  group_by(URM, Competency) |> 
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD = sd(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Competency, Mean), y = Mean, fill = URM)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Mean - SD, ymax = Mean + SD), 
                position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.2) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Aggregated OSCE Competency Scores by URM Status",
    x = "Competency Category",
    y = "Mean Score",
    fill = "URM Status"
  )

competency_summary

```

This grouped horizontal bar chart illustrates mean performance across the four aggregated OSCE competency categories (Oral Presentation, Communication, Medical Documentation, and Physical Examination), stratified by URM status. Mean scores and error bar spreads remain closely aligned between URM and non-URM groups across all four domains, with Oral Presentation showing the highest overall averages and Physical Examination recording slightly lower performance.




```{r, echo=FALSE}

competency_stat_table <- df_final |> 
  filter(URM %in% c("Non-URM", "URM")) |> 
  select(URM, all_of(ordered_osce)) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -URM,
    names_to = "Exam_Name",
    values_to = "Score"
  ) |> 
  mutate(Competency = case_when(
    grepl("Comm", Exam_Name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Communication Score",
    grepl("Phys|Physical", Exam_Name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Physical Exam Score",
    grepl("Med|Doc", Exam_Name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Medical Documentation",
    grepl("Oral|Pres", Exam_Name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Oral Presentation",
    TRUE ~ "Other"
  )) |> 
  filter(!is.na(Score)) |> 
  group_by(URM, Competency) |> 
  summarise(
    Mean   = mean(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD     = sd(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    IQR    = IQR(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    Min    = min(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max    = max(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    N_students  = n_distinct(df_final$ResearchID),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  arrange(Competency, URM)


competency_stat_table


```

This summary table presents descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, IQR, min, max, and student count) for the four aggregated OSCE competency categories stratified by URM status. Overall performance metrics remain high and closely comparable across both URM and non-URM groups across all competency domains.

Final Clerkship Grades-

Final Clerkship grades: PI mentions wanting to focus on the final clerkship grades. There is a lot of missingness for some final clerkship grades (AAC, RCC) and others have only one option heavily preferred of 'Pass' (EC, MSK)

<details>
<summary>Click to expand: Overall Table Summary For Final Clerkship Grades</summary>

```{r, echo=FALSE}
df_final_coursegrades <-  df_final |> 
  select(all_of(ends_with("_Final_Course_Grade")), 'URM') 

tbl_summary(df_final_coursegrades)
```

</details>

```{r, echo=FALSE}

urm_status_final_grades <- df_final_coursegrades |>    
  pivot_longer(
    cols = ends_with("_Final_Course_Grade"),
    names_to = "Final_Course",
    values_to = "Grade"
  ) |>    
  # Remove "_Final_Course_Grade" to leave just the course prefix
  mutate(Final_Course = gsub("_Final_Course_Grade", "", Final_Course)) |> 
  filter(URM %in% c("Non-URM", "URM"), !is.na(Grade)) |>   
  ggplot(aes(x = URM, fill = Grade)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge", alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ Final_Course) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Final Course Grades by URM Status",
    x = "URM Status",
    y = "Number of Students",
    fill = "Grade"
  )

urm_status_final_grades
```

This faceted bar chart illustrates the distribution of final course grades across pre-clerkship courses, stratified by URM status. Across most courses, grade distributions consistently span Pass, High Pass, and Honors categories for both groups.

USMLE scores-




```{r, echo=FALSE}
# ---- 4. USMLE scores by URM status table----
usmle_tbl <- df_final %>%
  mutate(URM = droplevels(URM)) %>% 
  filter(URM %in% c("Non-URM", "URM")) %>%
  select(URM, STEP1_ExamScore, STEP2CK_ExamScore) %>%
  tbl_summary(
    by = URM,
    label = list(STEP1_ExamScore ~ "USMLE Step 1", STEP2CK_ExamScore ~ "USMLE Step 2 CK"),
    type = all_continuous() ~ "continuous2",
    statistic = all_continuous() ~ c("{mean} ({sd})", "{median} [{p25}, {p75}]"),
    digits = all_continuous() ~ 1,
    missing_text = "Missing"
  ) %>%
  add_overall() %>%
  bold_labels()

usmle_tbl
```


These scores visually don't look like there is anything weird going on here - good!


```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

usmle_scores_prep  <- df_final |> select('STEP1_ExamScore', 'STEP2CK_ExamScore', 'URM')

  ggplot(aes(x = URM, y = Score, fill = URM)) +

usmle_plot
```

This boxplot figure displays the distribution of USMLE Step 1 and Step 2 CK exam scores stratified by URM status. For both examinations, median performance and interquartile ranges demonstrate overall consistent score distributions between URM and non-URM student groups.
